citation.title: OWASP Top 10 For Agentic Applications 2026
citation.publisher: OWASP Gen AI Security Project - Agentic Security Initiative
citation.reproduced: The codes ASI01-ASI10 and the ten risk names are reproduced from OWASP. Every description is this project's own paraphrase, not OWASP text (docs/audits/item9-owasp-asi-2026-source-check-2026-10-12.md, Correction 2, C2.3).

related.title: Agentic AI - Threats and Mitigations
related.relation: The foundational OWASP taxonomy (T-codes) that the Top 10 maps to and relies upon. It is a separate document: the ASI01-ASI10 codes belong to the Top 10, not to Threats and Mitigations.

ASI01.name: Agent Goal Hijack
ASI01.description: Attacker manipulates the agent's goals, instructions, or planning loop to redirect its behavior toward attacker-chosen objectives. Includes goal manipulation through prompt injection, instruction override, and planning corruption.

ASI02.name: Tool Misuse & Exploitation
ASI02.description: Adversaries cause the agent to invoke tools in unintended, unsafe, or unauthorized ways — covering tool poisoning, parameter injection, unauthorized tool invocation, and exploitation of tool implementation flaws.

ASI03.name: Identity & Privilege Abuse
ASI03.description: The agent acts under elevated identity or privilege, or attackers abuse the agent's identity to perform actions they could not otherwise perform — includes IAM misconfiguration, OAuth abuse, identity impersonation.

ASI04.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
ASI04.description: Compromise of dependencies in the agent stack: models, MCP servers, plugins, extensions, IDE components, datasets, packages — that propagate to agent behavior or data.

ASI05.name: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
ASI05.description: Agent-driven or agent-mediated execution of arbitrary code on host, container, or downstream systems — through tool calls, sandbox escapes, code interpreter abuse, or deserialization in agent runtimes.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.description: Persistent corruption of agent memory, knowledge bases, RAG stores, or context windows that biases or hijacks future behavior — both session-scoped and long-term memory variants.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.description: Vulnerabilities in agent-to-agent (A2A) protocols, message buses, MCP transport, or multi-agent coordination — including agent card poisoning, replay, impersonation, and broadcast amplification.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.description: Failure of one agent or agentic component propagates through multi-agent workflows, automated pipelines, or human-out-of-loop chains, amplifying impact.

ASI09.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
ASI09.description: Attackers exploit users' or operators' trust in the agent — through convincing but malicious output, social engineering of human-in-the-loop checkpoints, or manipulation of the agent's presentation layer.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.description: Agents acting autonomously in adversarial, unaligned, or malicious ways — whether intentionally weaponized (e.g., autonomous offensive agents) or emergent from misconfiguration.
